item.title: gAthA saptashatI
item.description:
Always used to think rAdhA legend is from brahma-vaivarta purANa and jayadeva’s gIta govinda

Oldest mention of Radha is around 2000 yrs old.

मुहमारुएण तं कण्ह गोरअं राहिआइ अवणेंतो ।
एआण वल्लवीणं अण्णाण वि गोरअं हरसि ॥
Krishna, as you blow the cow-dust off Radhika’s face with the breath of your mouth, you take away, from these other cowherd women, their pride as well.

This is from the Gatha Saptashati, a MH Prakrit poem from the Satavahana court dated to the first century.

item.title: Origins - sAtvata
item.description:
Source: TW

Exterior origin

The Pañcatantra “Viṣṇu as weaver” tale notably refers to Rādhā as the bhāryā (wife) of Viṣṇu, a rather perplexing statement given that “Rādhā” is not listed anywhere among the mahiṣīs of Kṛṣṇa.

Unlike Rukmiṇī, Jāmbavatī, Satyabhāmā, et al., she is entirely unknown to the Mahābhārata (including Harivaṃśa), Viṣṇupurāṇa, Bhāgavatapurāṇa, etc.

viShAkhA

In my opinion, Rādhā likely originated as a minor Śākta goddess possibly associated with nakṣatra viśākhā (cf. “rādhe viśākhe suhavā ’nurādhā”).

item.title: PAncharAtra connection
item.description:
Source: TW

Here is an archana procedure in chapters 26,27,28,29 (of skanda purANa). Looks like the section might have been incorporated into the text from a Pancharatric manual from a region where Her worship was already canon. Very rich avarana puja and specific bahyapuja. Also curiously the mūlamantra deployed seems to be Dvadashakshari(along with Shadaksnari and Ashtakshari) which is a given for a Pancharatric lineage.

Perhaps either Maharashtra or Utkala/Vanga regions.
